answer: Attackers must forge distinct attestations or acquire fresh embers, and a raven audit committee randomly samples identities each epoch, slashing duplicates. A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to burn a unique on-chain ember token tied to a verified proof-of-personhood attestation, so spawning fake participants costs real stake per identity. Mass sybil creation then becomes economically self-defeating: the cost of each ember plus slashing risk exceeds any reward, deterring forgery at scale. From sa0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
